one_line: User gives only an email at start; agent must authenticate via find_user_id_by_email before anything else.
User can't recall email, gives name+zip instead; agent authenticates via find_user_id_by_name_zip.
Already-authenticated user asks status of a specific order id; correct move is a plain get_order_details lookup.
Authenticated user asks what payment methods are on file; correct move is get_user_details, not an order lookup.
User asks if a specific item from a delivered order is still in stock; correct move is get_item_details on that item id.
User asks about other finishes/sizes of a product they own one variant of; correct move is get_product_details.
User has several orders but only one pending; asks to cancel 'the pending one' by mistake, unambiguous target.
Authenticated user with one pending order requests a shipping address change on that order after moving.
User with one pending order and two credit cards asks to switch the order's payment to the other card.
User negotiates a color swap on a pending Bluetooth Speaker item across turns, confirms exact new item id and card.
User asks to return one identified item (mechanical keyboard) from a multi-item delivered order, refund to paypal.
Multi-turn size exchange negotiation on delivered running shoes order resolves to a specific variant and refund.
User with single pending tea kettle order asks to cancel because they no longer need it.
User explicitly asks to update their account-level default address, distinct from any specific order's address.
User returns one item (leaking tea kettle) from a two-item delivered order, refund redirected to a different gift card.
User authenticated by name+zip (no email) asks to move their one pending order's payment from gift card to credit card.
User asks to cancel own pending order but also asks agent to cancel a roommate's order id; only own order is actioned.
User with a pending and a delivered order both listed asks to cancel 'the one with the skateboard', resolves to pending order.
